rootCauses.cause: Token get does not distinguish the original Integer/Long input from the Decimal string/typed read view. Dynamic put round-trips the input through Decimal storage, destroying the original scalar identity.
rootCauses.proposal: Retain input scalar identity for the captured caller-owned writes; project token reads separately from string/typed reads. Row 011 requires original Integer identity even after a string put. Leave constructor, boxed/string get, queried and trigger Decimal views unchanged. Capture token reads after typed/constructor writes and after DML before extending that projection.

rootCauses.cause: coerceCast rejects boxed Decimal-to-Integer but has no corresponding boxed Decimal-to-Long guard. Its fallback explicitly converts a Decimal into Long even when the expression is statically Object.
rootCauses.proposal: Reject the captured Object-held Decimal-to-Long cast before numeric conversion; preserve direct statically Decimal field casts (077-094), Integer widening (001/004/011/054/055/057/059/061), token Long widening (006), and null controls. Do not change all numeric casts or field types.

rootCauses.cause: Ordinary custom Decimal-field dynamic put has no String/Boolean type check; numeric checks at this dispatcher are restricted to platform events. Storage conversion falls back to the supplied scalar rather than rejecting it.
rootCauses.proposal: Apply the captured Number-field String/Boolean rejection at dynamic put, preserving numeric and null writes. Assert native SObjectException wording; broader String coercion or other field categories need captures.

rootCauses.cause: String put normalizes Long into Decimal, and DML serializes that Decimal without knowing the original dynamic Long input. Native reads Decimal but rejects these two Long inputs at insert before any trigger observation.
rootCauses.proposal: Preserve dynamic-write origin independently from the visible Decimal view and reject the two captured Long insert inputs using the native INVALID_TYPE_ON_FIELD_IN_RECORD error. Typed Long assignment remains accepted (017/022/024/026/048) and constructor Long remains accepted for the captured in-memory read (018), which does not establish constructor-Long DML behavior. Do not blanket-reject Long fields or infer the boundary from a field name. Capture other numeric fields, update and overwrite transitions before extending the rule.

rootCauses.cause: SUM always appends .0 to an integral aggregate result. The captured crossing sum is Decimal text/JSON 2147483648, while small sums 053/056 return 3.0.
rootCauses.proposal: Repair the SUM result rendering only after a native boundary sweep explains why this captured total loses .0. Proposed next captures: sums 2147483646/2147483647/2147483648/2147483649 and negative twins, different input scales, and anonymous/isTest at 62/67/68. Do not infer an Integer-size threshold from these two totals.
